insights.title: The sport-invariance gate is a ceiling, and the old bar sat under the floor
insights.body: G2 asks a classifier to name a row's sport from its joint vector, and LOWER is better: the target is a ceiling, met when accuracy falls below it. The three classes are 12,966 / 5,323 / 2,430, so always answering 'hoops' scores 0.6258 -- and a globally shuffled embedding scores 0.6257, confirming that 0.6258 is the floor any embedding lands on, including a perfectly sport-blind one. The retired 0.4333 target came from '1/3 + 0.10', which assumed balanced classes. It was UNREACHABLE: nothing could satisfy it, and a trivial majority-class predictor fails it. The fix replaced an impossible bar with an achievable one (0.6258 + 0.10 = 0.7258), it did not relax a bar to buy a pass. The model scores 0.6851, so the status reads 'met' -- but the file itself calls that weak, and the number that carries information is g2_delta_vs_majority = 0.0593. Sport identity is still partly recoverable from the joint vector.
insights.source: assets/unified.json -> g2_sport_acc / g2_target / g2_majority_baseline / g2_delta_vs_majority / g2_status / g2_note; data/stage2_report.json -> g2.SUPERSEDED_g2_target_chance_plus_10; data/gate_nonvacuity.json -> g2_null_lands_at_floor and g2_baseline_correction

insights.title: A gate that read 0.0 for months, and what it reads now
insights.body: G1 checks that joining the three sports does not cost each one its own structure, comparing a per-sport baseline against the joint space. Its position arm reported a drop of exactly 0.0 for all three sports from Phase 2 until 2026-08-03 -- not because nothing changed, but because the accuracy helper used the int64 position mask as an INDEX rather than a mask, so both arms scored exactly 1.0 and their difference was 0.0 by construction. Re-exporting could not fix it: the verdict is read straight from the checkpoint, so the buggy value reproduces forever. The shipped asset now substitutes measured values from a separate probe. Convention is baseline minus joint, so negative means the joint space is better: hoops -0.0526 (0.7385 -> 0.7911), gridiron 0.0000 (0.9991, already at ceiling), pitch +0.0021 (0.8930 -> 0.8909). A globally shuffled embedding drops +0.5493 / +0.6920 / +0.5617, so the pass now rests on evidence rather than on a constant.
insights.source: assets/unified.json -> g1_verdict (per-sport pos_drop / pos_baseline_e_s / pos_joint_z) and g1_pos_caveat; data/g1_position_probe.json; data/stage2_report.json -> verdict_from_train (still shows the stale 0.0)

insights.title: Six of the twelve archetypes are declared and never assigned
insights.body: The taxonomy lists A0 through A11, but only A0, A1, A2, A3, A5 and A11 appear on any of the 20,719 rows; A4 and A6 through A10 have zero members. The reasons are measured, not hand-waved. A4 (defensive disruptor / ball-hawk) had pitch-only members -- one native cluster, 81% defenders, with no hoops or gridiron counterpart -- so cross-sport analogy for it was trivially impossible and scored 0.000; that cluster now folds into A3, which does span hoops interior defenders and pitch defenders. A6/A7 (pedigree) and A8/A9 (career arc) were the wrong grain: they describe how a career is going, a per-career label, while A0-A5 describe what a player does in a season. They have since been split onto a separate trajectory axis as T0-T3, with zero members in scope for v0 because the pedigree join they need is not available for all three sports -- and the join itself is booby-trapped: matching pedigree by normalised name across the whole set produced 17 matches, all 17 false positives, including an NFL Matt Ryan matched to an NBA Matt Ryan.
insights.source: data/archetype_map.json -> archetypes_deferred_v0, scope_note_v0, axes.blast_radius_measured, axes.trajectory.join_caveat_MEASURED; data/unified_meta.json -> arch_counts (A4: 0)

insights.title: The automated role check works; the hand-picked pairs do not
insights.body: Two different analogy measurements disagree, and both are reported. Run across all 20,719 rows, a player's nearest neighbour in another sport carries the same archetype 98.28% of the time against a 0.1712 random baseline -- and that 0.60 bar is a real bar, unlike G2's 1/3, because the baseline was actually computed from the archetype mix. But ask the model to retrieve a specific named counterpart -- Tom Brady's Stephen Curry, Derrick Henry's Joel Embiid -- and it fails completely: 0 of 40 curated pairs land in the top 10, and the mean rank of the target is 2,114 against a random expectation of 2,067, a ratio of 0.978 that is indistinguishable from chance and if anything slightly worse. An earlier version of this file quoted 3.287x as a salvage; that used N/2 as the random rank when the correct expectation for a minimum over k draws is (N-k)/(k+1). What survives is coarse archetype agreement on those pairs: 0.65 against a 0.1621 baseline. The space knows the role. It does not know the person.
insights.source: data/analogy_report.json -> G4_cross_sport_nn_role_coherence; data/analogy_triples_report.json -> retrieval_top10_hit_rate_informational, mean_b_rank, random_expected_rank, better_than_random_ratio, SUPERSEDED_better_than_random_ratio, baseline_correction_note, G4_curated_arch_agreement, arch_agreement_random_baseline; data/gate_nonvacuity.json -> g4_baseline

insights.title: Tennis was probed as a fourth sport and deliberately left out
insights.body: A fourth sport was tested before being excluded, and the probe says why. Over 4,022 tennis player-seasons, the first principal component takes 37.5% of the variance and loads on WIN_RATE (0.41), DRAW_PROGRESS_MEAN (0.402) and GAMES_WON_PCT (0.397) -- it reads as quality, not role. Even after projecting the quality axis out and re-clustering, the verdict is QUALITY TIERING: the clusters separate on how good a player is, not on what kind of player they are, which is a different question from the one A0-A11 answer. Admitting them would have repeated the exact role-versus-trajectory category error the archetype axes were just split to fix. One cluster of the six (n=487, dominated by SURFACE_SPECIALISATION at z=1.655 with flat quality) does look role-like and is flagged rather than discarded. The file proposes no archetype names at all, on the grounds that naming a k-means partition would launder it into a taxonomy.
insights.source: data/tennis_archetype_probe.json -> verdict, pc1_variance_share, pc1_top_loadings, pc1_reads_as_quality, role_like_clusters, per_cluster.4, naming_note, method_note

caveat: Every number here is read from the listed files; nothing is estimated. Three things to hold onto. (1) The joint space is not fully sport-blind -- a classifier still beats a majority-class guess by 0.0593, and the gate status of 'met' only means 'within ten points of a floor anyone hits by guessing'. (2) The G3 archetype separation is real but partly confounded: the within-archetype and between-archetype samples draw different mixes of sport pairs, with a composition gap of up to 8.9 percentage points, so some of that separation is a sport-pair effect rather than an archetype effect; the file states the confound is present without claiming how much. (3) The Split Decision game compares raw VOR deltas across two sports whose VOR scales differ substantially -- hoops careers span a much wider range than gridiron ones -- so a larger hoops number is not evidence that a hoops career improved more in any absolute sense. Direction labels also come from a narrower population than 'all careers': VOR is floored at zero, so 287 hoops and 340 gridiron careers spent entirely below replacement are dropped rather than labelled, because 'bad then bad' is not a direction.

game.prompt: Split Decision: one basketball career, one football career. Which one rose more from the first half of its career to the second?
game.axis_label: Career VOR delta (second-half mean minus first-half mean)
game.explainer: Each career is split down the middle and scored on value over replacement. The delta is the second-half mean minus the first-half mean, so positive means the player got better and negative means they fell off. Careers under 4 seasons are excluded, as are careers spent entirely below replacement. Watch the sport labels: hoops VOR runs on a wider scale than gridiron VOR, so the comparison is between two numbers the model computed the same way, not between two equally-sized worlds.

rounds.reveal: curry over 16 seasons: 13.03 in the first half, 14.04 in the second, a delta of +1.01, which the model leaves unlabelled rather than calling it a rise. henry over 10 seasons: 3.05 to 6.56, a delta of +3.51, labelled D0 rising.
mcbride has only 4 seasons scored, going 0.47 to 6.60 for a delta of +6.13. leonard has 13, going 10.15 to 17.38 for +7.23. Both are labelled D0 rising.

Both went down, so the larger delta is the smaller fall. james across 23 seasons: 24.32 in the first half, 20.93 in the second, a delta of -3.39, labelled D1 declining. brady across 21 seasons: 2.66 to 1.87, a delta of -0.79, small enough that the model leaves him unlabelled.
Two collapses. beckham over 9 seasons: 9.08 down to 0.07. carter over 22 seasons: 13.12 down to 0.88. beckham's delta of -9.01 is the larger of the two; both are labelled D1 declining.

tatum over 9 seasons: 6.65 to 16.91, a delta of +10.26. london has the minimum 4 seasons and scores 0.00 in his first half, so his entire 5.30 second-half value reads as the delta. Both are labelled D0 rising.

jefferson over 6 seasons: 7.41 to 5.25, a delta of -2.16, labelled D1 declining. embiid over 10 seasons: 27.89 to 29.20, a delta of +1.31 that is small enough to leave him unlabelled despite both halves being high.

A near tie in the wrong direction. elliott over 9 seasons: 8.82 to 1.05, a delta of -7.77. westbrook over 18 seasons: 20.46 to 13.25, a delta of -7.22. Both are labelled D1 declining, separated by 0.55.

adams over 12 seasons: 3.93 to 7.43, a delta of +3.49. doncic over 8 seasons: 24.58 to 28.52, a delta of +3.94. Both are labelled D0 rising, and they land within half a point of each other from very different starting levels.
haliburton has 5 seasons scored: 2.13 to 14.42, a delta of +12.29. jacobs has 7: 2.47 to 4.35, a delta of +1.88. Both are labelled D0 rising.
kupp over 9 seasons: 2.90 to 5.88, a delta of +2.99. bryant over 19 seasons: 12.22 to 15.14, a delta of +2.92. Seven hundredths apart, and both are labelled D0 rising.
Both declined, so the larger delta is the gentler drop. kamara over 9 seasons: 9.46 to 4.03, a delta of -5.43. wade over 16 seasons: 19.89 to 11.32, a delta of -8.57. Both are labelled D1 declining.
